title: Physiological functions in animals
blurb: Part 1, from cells to a body: unicellular vs multicellular; the hierarchy cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → body; the 4 animal tissue types; unitary vs modular organisms; new bodies by asexual reproduction or from a fertilised egg (zygote → morula → blastula → gastrula); 3 germ layers; body plans (Hydra and jellyfish with 2 germ layers; acoelomate flatworms, pseudocoelomate roundworms, coelomate annelids); radial vs bilateral symmetry; the main body functions.
lede: Part 1, from cells to a body: unicellular vs multicellular; the hierarchy cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → body; the 4 animal tissue types; unitary vs modular organisms; new bodies by asexual reproduction or from a fertilised egg (zygote → morula → blastula → gastrula); 3 germ layers; body plans (Hydra and jellyfish with 2 germ layers; acoelomate flatworms, pseudocoelomate roundworms, coelomate annelids); radial vs bilateral symmetry; the main body functions. Part 2, the interplay of organ systems, compared across animals: respiration (skin, gills, lungs, tracheae, tracheal gills, haemoglobin), circulation (open with haemolymph vs closed with blood; single vs double loop; heart chambers from fish to mammals; capillaries; blood cells; haemoglobin), nervous systems (neuron; nerve net → nerve cords → brain) and digestion (gastrovascular cavity vs tract; insects, crayfish, spider, molluscs, vertebrates; pyloric caeca, the hen's crop and gizzard, the ruminant 4-part stomach; liver and gall bladder; symbiotic microorganisms).
six: Organisation hierarchy and the 4 tissue types
Zygote → morula → blastula → gastrula; three germ layers; Hydra and jellyfish have two
Main body functions (reproduction matters for the population, not the individual)
Respiratory structures by group (tracheae and spiracles in insects; epidermis in earthworms; air sacs in birds)

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four basic animal tissue types?
questions.e: The four are epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous. (Slides: p. 9)

questions.q: The correct order of early embryonic stages is:

questions.e: Hydra stays at the gastrula level with two layers. (Slides: p. 19)

questions.q: Roundworms have which type of body cavity?
Which animals have an open circulatory system?
questions.e: Insects, crustaceans and mussels: open system with haemolymph. (Slides: p. 47–49)
Amphibians: 2 atria + 1 ventricle with mixed blood. (Slides: p. 54)

questions.q: The nervous system of cnidarians is a:
questions.e: Cnidarians have a nerve net. (Slides: p. 62)

questions.q: Malpighian tubules belong to the excretory system of:
questions.e: They join the insect gut between midgut and hindgut. (Slides: p. 65)

questions.q: Which is NOT a chamber of the ruminant stomach?
questions.e: Rumen, reticulum, omasum, abomasum; the gizzard is in birds. (Slides: p. 72, p. 74)

questions.q: Which organ stores and concentrates bile?
questions.e: The liver makes bile; the gall bladder stores and concentrates it. (Slides: p. 73)

questions.q: Which animals have no definite respiratory system?
questions.e: Gas exchange through the epidermis. (Slides: p. 30)

cards.lede: Read the question, answer it out loud, then flip the card.

items.a: In the correct sense (adult stage), animals are always multicellular.
Cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → body.
Ligaments/tendons, loose connective tissue, adipose tissue, cartilage, bone, blood.

items.n: Four kinds of neurons by shape?

items.a: Unitary: clearly defined body (fish, mammal). Modular: colony of autonomous modules (sponges, corals).

items.n: First stages of development from a fertilised egg?
How many germ layers do Hydra and jellyfish have?
items.a: Two: ectoderm and endoderm (Hydra stays at the gastrula level).

items.n: Why is reproduction special among body functions?
items.a: It isn't needed for the individual's survival, only for the population's.

items.n: Which animals lack a definite respiratory system?
items.a: Planarians and earthworms; they exchange gases through the epidermis.

items.n: What serves as gills in Alitta virens?
Where are the gills of the water flea?

items.a: Through tracheae and tracheoles that open via spiracles (plus air sacs).

items.n: How do aquatic insect larvae breathe?
What do birds have besides lungs?

items.a: Open: haemolymph in sinuses (insects, crustaceans, mussels). Closed: blood in vessels (annelids, cephalopods, vertebrates).
Openings in the insect heart through which haemolymph returns.

items.n: How does fluid move at a capillary?
items.a: Squeezed out by blood pressure at the arterial end; re-enters by osmotic attraction at the venous end.
1 atrium + 1 ventricle; single loop through the gills.
2 atria + 1 ventricle; blood mixes in the ventricle.

items.n: Which vertebrates have a fully divided 4-chambered heart?

items.a: Erythrocytes, monocytes, lymphocytes, neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils, platelets.
2 α + 2 β chains, each with a heme (Fe-protoporphyrin IX) holding iron.

items.n: Parts of a neuron and impulse direction?
What is special about the squid's nervous system?

items.a: A digestive cavity with one opening serving as mouth and anus (Hydra, Planaria).

items.n: Three parts of the insect gut?
Parts of the crayfish digestive tract?

items.a: Many blind "intestines" around the stomach of trout, for food absorption.

items.n: What are the crop and gizzard?
items.a: Parts of the bird gut: crop stores food, gizzard (ventriculus) grinds it.

items.n: Role of the liver and gall bladder?
items.a: Liver = biochemical factory, produces bile; the gall bladder stores and concentrates bile.

items.n: Four parts of a ruminant stomach?
Who digests cellulose for ruminants and termites?
